text.p: A group of Florida physicians said Monday it was scuttling plans to form a statewide health maintenance organization after failing to raise the funds needed to get the group off the ground.

Executives for Doctors' Health Plan, a Jacksonville-based company, called off a six-month effort to raise $30 million in capitalization funds after collecting only $2.4 million from 351 physician investors.

Company officials, who received approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission in June to begin soliciting investors, cited a fiercely competitive market for their failure to raise the necessary cash.

"The low response was clearly due to the volatile, highly competitive nature of the managed care industry and the advent of managed care plans in the Florida market over the past 18 months," Doctors' Health Plan Chairman Dr. Charles Hayes said in a statement.

In June, the company began offering stock at $10 a share to members of the Florida Medical Association and the Florida Osteopathic Medical Association. Investors, who could purchase a maximum of 5,000 shares, would become providers in the plan, which was scheduled to become operational this year.
Facing competition from such HMO giants as Blue Cross/Blue Shield and United Health Care, physicians were not ready to support another managed care product, said company spokesman Jack MacAbee.

"The consolidation trend really picked up over the past year, with bigger companies getting bigger and new companies jumping in," MacAbee said. "Doctors asked themselves, 'Can DHP really be competitive?'"
